key_insight: Generic machine learning identified baseline risk clusters for intensive blood pressure control, but it did not show meaningful treatment effect heterogeneity across groups.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest that individualized benefit predictions for intensive BP lowering should be interpreted cautiously because average benefit was modest and subgroup differences were not statistically significant.
method: Pooled participant-level data from two large randomized blood pressure control trials.
Applied the model-free GenericML framework with robust estimators: Best Linear Predictor (BLP), Group Average Treatment Effects (GATES), and baseline profile classification (CLAN).
Compared predicted-benefit strata and tested whether treatment response differed across groups.
evidence_signal: Analysis included 10,712 participants followed for up to 3 years; intensive BP control showed a small average risk reduction, but HTE tests were non-significant (BLP p=0.443; GATES p=0.471).
watch_item: Machine-learning risk clusters may look clinically plausible, but without statistically supported subgroup effects they should not be used to guide individualized treatment decisions.
paper_title: Revisiting the High-Benefit Patient: Generic Machine Learning Inference for Intensive Blood Pressure Control
